title: Observability deployment operator for VPCs: terraform module, canary upgrades, and health probes
creator: Asha Khanna
description: Build a reusable Terraform module and a lightweight deployment operator that installs and upgrades the VPC observability stack (Prometheus + Grafana metrics, OpenTelemetry collector, and log export pipeline) with production-safe canary upgrades and automated health probes. This ticket covers module API design, secret/KMS integration patterns, canary rollout hooks, healthcheck definitions, and the acceptance tests for upgrades and rollback behavior. Goal: single terraform module + small operator CRDs to apply upgrades, perform health validation, and reconcile drift for Private (VPC) deployments.
progress_updates: 2026-03-10 - Kickoff: design reviewed with PM (Diego Morales) and infra (Priya Nair). Agreed on goals: idempotent Terraform module, operator to handle online upgrades where possible.
2026-03-11 - Prototype: created initial terraform module scaffold with submodules for metrics, traces, and logs. Pushed branch feat/eng/527890/obs-operator (GH: redwood/infra#2147).

2026-03-12 - Design decision: choose OpenTelemetry Collector + Vector as sidecar replacement for fluent-bit due to consistent processor model and easier metric extraction. Noted trade-offs in description document.
2026-03-12 - Blocker identified: RBAC for operator service account requires cross-account IAM role in some customer VPCs; added dependency ENG-527891 to implement IAM role assumption helper module.
technical_notes: Module layout: modules/observability/{metrics,otlp,logging}-each with variables.tf, outputs.tf, examples/
State handling: recommend remote state per-environment (S3 + state locking) and an import path for existing Prometheus/Grafana resources to avoid duplicate deployments.

Secrets: use customer KMS with envelope encryption. Terraform variables accept kms_key_arn and operator mounts KMS credentials via secret provider interface (SPIFFE/SecretManager integrations documented).

Canary upgrades: operator will perform a phased upgrade – create parallel resources in canary namespace, run health probes for N minutes, run smoke queries against Prometheus and Grafana dashboards, then switch traffic and teardown old resources.

Health probes: liveness/readiness for OTEL/Vector agents, sample scrape validation for Prometheus (scrape success ratio > 99% over 5 min), grafana provisioning check, log pipeline delivery latency < 60s for test events.
Rollback: keep previous configuration and PV snapshots for grafana; automated rollback triggered if health probes fail during canary windows. Manual approval gate for global switch.
Observability of the operator: expose operator metrics (upgrade_duration_seconds, canary_failure_total, drift_reconcile_count) to a control-plane Prometheus target.
Compatibility: module supports k8s >=1.26 and eks >=1.24. Provide a compatibility matrix in README.

Cost controls: default retention and downsampling: Prometheus TSDB retention 7d for private deployments; recommend cheaper long-term storage via remote_write to Cortex/Thanos controlled by var remote_write_enabled.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes clear variables for namespace, storage class, retention, KMS key, and log destinations.
Operator can perform a canary upgrade within a single VPC cluster and automatically promote when health checks pass.
Automated health probes detect failures and trigger rollback during upgrade tests in CI.
Documentation (README + runbook) exists with manual rollback steps and KMS onboarding instructions.
E2E tests in CI simulate a failed canary and validate automated rollback behavior.
testing_plan: Unit tests: terraform validate and tflint for module code.
Integration: deploy module in ephemeral test VPC (CI) and run canary upgrade scenario using test harness.
Chaos tests: introduce network partition to collector and verify health probe triggers and rollback.
Performance: validate Prometheus scrape throughput at expected customer scale (1000 targets) in perf lab.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge module and operator to canary branch.
2) Run CI integration tests deploying to ephemeral cluster and exercising canary upgrade flow.
3) Deploy to internal staging VPC and run 72h soak with synthetic load. Monitor operator metrics.
4) Offer beta to one existing Dedicated/private customer behind feature flag; do manual supervised upgrade.
5) Gradual ramp to production for all new Private deployments and provide migration path for existing customers.
